subproblem.title: Flat flux identity: ∫ of D_eφ over the half-space {⟨y,e⟩ > 0} equals −∫_{e^⊥} φ dHⁿ
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, N := n + 1, ℝ^N = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N), e ∈ ℝ^N with |e| = 1, H := {y ∈ ℝ^N : ⟨y, e⟩ > 0}, P := (span{e})^⊥ and Hⁿ := μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N). Let φ : ℝ^N → ℝ be C¹ with compact support. Then ∫_H Dφ(y)e dL^N(y) = −∫_P φ dHⁿ. Here Dφ(y)e = fderiv ℝ φ y e, L^N = volume, and ∫_H, ∫_P are integrals against the restricted measures L^N⌞H and Hⁿ⌞P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (e : Rn (n + 1)) (φ : Rn (n + 1) → ℝ), ‖e‖ = 1 → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → HasCompactSupport φ → ∫ y in {y : Rn (n + 1) | 0 < inner ℝ y e}, fderiv ℝ φ y e = -∫ y in ((Submodule.span ℝ {e})ᗮ : Set (Rn (n + 1))), φ y ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the supplied parent proof, Step 1 (flat facts), second paragraph: 'since (d/dt)φ(T(z, t)) = D_eφ(T(z, t)), Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus (φ has compact support) give ∫_H D_eφ dL^N = ∫_{ℝⁿ} ∫_0^∞ (d/dt)φ(T(z, t)) dt dz = ∫_{ℝⁿ} (−φ(T(z, 0))) dz = −∫_P φ dHⁿ'. It is the flat identity used implicitly in the last step of Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 4.3 (chapter-03.txt lines 739-746: 'by 4.1, (1) and (2) we have μ_{ρ⁻¹E} → Hⁿ⌞{x^{n+1} = 0}'), with the limit half-space {⟨y, e⟩ > 0} fixed by the sign correction E1. The coordinates T(z, t) = ι(z) + te of the supplied proof are realized below by the orthogonal decomposition ℝ^N = span{e} ⊕ P. This is the same Fubini/FTC argument.

Notation. V := ℝ^N, L := span{e}, P := L^⊥, H := {y : ⟨y, e⟩ > 0}, ψ(y) := Dφ(y)e. For a finite-dimensional inner product space W, L_W denotes its Lebesgue (volume) measure.

1. Preliminaries. Since |e| = 1 we have e ≠ 0, and dim V = n + 1 (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so dim P = n (Submodule.finrank_orthogonal_span_singleton). H is the preimage of (0, ∞) under the continuous map y ↦ ⟨y, e⟩, so it is open, hence Borel. Since φ is C¹, y ↦ Dφ(y) is continuous, so ψ is continuous. If ψ(y) ≠ 0 then Dφ(y) ≠ 0, so tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport φ and ψ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply). Hence ψ and 1_H ψ are L_V-integrable, and ∫_H ψ dL_V = ∫_V 1_H ψ dL_V (integral_indicator).

2. Product decomposition and Fubini. Let Φ : V → L × P, Φ(y) := (π_L(y), π_P(y)) (orthogonal projections). Φ is a measurable equivalence with Φ⁻¹(l, p) = (l + p) +ᵥ 0 = l + p (Submodule.measurableEquivProd with base point 0; Submodule.measurableEquivProd_symm_apply). It is measure preserving from μHE[dim V] on V to the product measure L_L ⊗ L_P (Submodule.measurePreserving_measurableEquivProd). Since μHE[dim V] = L_V (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), Φ and Φ⁻¹ are measure preserving between L_V and L_L ⊗ L_P. Hence ∫_V 1_H ψ dL_V = ∫_{L×P} 1_H ψ(l + p) d(L_L ⊗ L_P)(l, p) (MeasurePreserving.integral_comp' for the measurable equivalence Φ⁻¹). The integrand (l, p) ↦ 1_H ψ(l + p) is L_L ⊗ L_P-integrable: it is the integrable function 1_H ψ composed with the measure-preserving measurable embedding Φ⁻¹ (MeasurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb). So Fubini (integral_prod_symm) gives
 ∫_H ψ dL_V = ∫_P ( ∫_L 1_H ψ(l + p) dL_L(l) ) dL_P(p).

3. Reduction of the inner integral to a half-line. Fix p ∈ P. Since |e| = 1, T : ℝ → L, T(t) := te, is a linear isometric equivalence (LinearIsometryEquiv.toSpanUnitSingleton). Hence it is measure preserving from L¹ to L_L (LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving), and it is a measurable embedding because it is a homeomorphism. Therefore ∫_L 1_H ψ(l + p) dL_L(l) = ∫_ℝ 1_H ψ(te + p) dt (MeasurePreserving.integral_comp). As p ∈ (span{e})^⊥, ⟨p, e⟩ = 0, so ⟨te + p, e⟩ = t|e|² + ⟨p, e⟩ = t. Thus te + p ∈ H iff t > 0, so 1_H ψ(te + p) = 1_{(0,∞)}(t) ψ(te + p), and
 ∫_L 1_H ψ(l + p) dL_L(l) = ∫_{(0,∞)} ψ(te + p) dt (integral_indicator for the Borel set (0, ∞)).

4. Fundamental theorem of calculus on the half-line. Let c(t) := te + p and h := φ ∘ c.
 - Since |c(s) − c(t)| = |s − t||e| = |s − t|, c : ℝ → V is an isometry, hence a closed embedding (ℝ is complete).
 - c has derivative e at every t and φ has derivative Dφ(c(t)) at c(t), so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) h'(t) = Dφ(c(t))e = ψ(c(t)) for every t ∈ ℝ.
 - h = φ∘c and ψ∘c are continuous with compact support, because compact support pulls back along the closed embedding c (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding).
 - Hence ψ∘c is integrable on (0, ∞), and h is continuous on [0, ∞) at 0.
 - h(t) → 0 as t → +∞: a compactly supported function tends to 0 along the cocompact filter (HasCompactSupport.is_zero_at_infty), and atTop ≤ cocompact on ℝ.
 The improper FTC (integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto, with a = 0 and limit 0) gives
 ∫_{(0,∞)} ψ(te + p) dt = 0 − h(0) = −φ(p).

5. Hⁿ⌞P is Lebesgue measure on P. The inclusion ι : P → V is an isometry with range P, so the push-forward under ι of μHE[n] on P is μHE[n]⌞P (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). On P, dim P = n by step 1, so μHE[n] = μHE[dim P] = L_P (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). P is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed and Borel, so ι is a measurable embedding (MeasurableEmbedding.subtype_coe). Therefore ∫_P φ dHⁿ = ∫_V φ d(ι_# L_P) = ∫_P φ(p) dL_P(p) (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).

6. Conclusion. By steps 2-4, ∫_H ψ dL_V = ∫_P (−φ(p)) dL_P(p) = −∫_P φ(p) dL_P(p) (integral_neg). By step 5 this equals −∫_P φ dHⁿ, i.e. ∫_H Dφ(y)e dL^N(y) = −∫_P φ dHⁿ. For n = 0 we have P = {0}, L_P is the unit point mass, and the identity reads ∫_H ψ = −φ(0); steps 1-6 cover this case unchanged. ∎
proof_key_steps: dim P = n. ψ = Dφ(·)e is continuous with compact support, so ∫_H ψ = ∫ 1_H ψ with 1_H ψ integrable.
The measure-preserving orthogonal decomposition Φ : ℝ^N ≅ span{e} × P (Submodule.measurableEquivProd, μHE[N] = volume) plus Fubini give ∫_H ψ = ∫_P ∫_{span{e}} 1_H ψ(l + p) dl dp.
T(t) = te is a measure-preserving isometry ℝ ≅ span{e}. For p ⊥ e, ⟨te + p, e⟩ = t, so the inner integral is ∫_0^∞ ψ(te + p) dt.
The improper FTC for h(t) = φ(te + p), with h' = ψ(te + p) and compact support along the isometric line, gives inner integral −φ(p).
Hⁿ⌞P is the push-forward of vol_P under the isometric inclusion (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and μHE[n] = volume on P). Hence ∫_H ψ = −∫_P φ dHⁿ.
